key_insight: DLAM learns latent actions as distributions rather than fixed codes, making action representations more robust for predicting future changes from video and for aligning with robot actions. By adding temporal constraints, it aims to capture when transitions happen without relying on brittle deterministic transition points.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of action-labeled robot data by using abundant action-free videos to learn useful action priors, while overcoming the weakness of reconstruction-trained and deterministic latent action methods that struggle to generalize and jointly generate with real robot actions.
method: Learn distributional latent actions from action-free video, so each latent action can represent uncertainty and variation in transitions.
Introduce temporal constraints to better align inferred transitions with time and reduce errors from locally inferred transition points.
Design the latent action space to support joint generation/prediction with robot actions rather than only reconstructing observed video frames.
impact: This approach can make vision-language-action systems more data-efficient by leveraging unlabeled video at scale. For practitioners, it offers a more reliable way to transfer knowledge from passive video observations to real robot control.
